outlooks.summary: SCATTERED SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS WILL DEVELOP ACROSS THE CENTRAL AND NORTHERN ROCKIES AND EASTWARD INTO THE PLAINS OF EASTERN MONTANA...THE WESTERN DAKOTAS...WESTERN KANSAS AND THE TEXAS AND OKLAHOMA PANHANDLES. LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND GUSTS WILL BE THE MAIN SEVERE THREATS PRIMARILY FROM MID AFTERNOON INTO THE EVENING HOURS.

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: SYNOPTIC PATTERN WILL REMAIN PROGRESSIVE THURSDAY WITH UPPER TROUGH NOW MOVING THROUGH THE PACIFIC NW AND CA CONTINUING INTO THE CNTRL AND NRN ROCKIES. LOW-AMPLITUDE UPPER RIDGE SHOULD PERSIST OVER THE PLAINS DOWNSTREAM FROM THIS FEATURE WITH WEAK PERTURBATIONS MOVING THROUGH THE RIDGE. ELSEWHERE...A LOW AMPLITUDE TROUGH WILL CONTINUE INTO THE NERN STATES ALONG WITH A SLOW MOVING UPPER LOW CIRCULATION OVER THE WRN GULF AND LOWER MS VALLEY AREA. AT THE SFC A LEE TROUGH WILL RESIDE ACROSS THE HIGH PLAINS.

sections.title: SRN...CNTRL THROUGH NRN HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: SLY LOW-LEVEL JET WILL PERSIST OVER THE HIGH PLAINS IN ASSOCIATION WITH LEE TROUGH. RICHER GULF MOISTURE WITH MID-UPPER 60S DEWPOINTS WILL ADVECT NWD BENEATH STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES RESULTING IN AN AXIS OF MODERATE TO STRONG INSTABILITY /2000-3000 J/KG MLCAPE/. A LEAD VORTICITY MAXIMUM EMBEDDED WITHIN THE UPPER TROUGH WILL MOVE INTO WRN MT THURSDAY MORNING AND CONTINUE THROUGH CNTRL MT DURING THE AFTERNOON. THUNDERSTORMS WILL LIKELY DEVELOP OVER THE HIGHER TERRAIN OF WRN/CNTRL MT AND NRN WY AND SUBSEQUENTLY SPREAD INTO THE HIGH PLAINS. ADDITIONAL STORMS WILL LIKELY DEVELOP BY MID-LATE AFTERNOON OVER THE HIGHER TERRAIN OF CO AND WY. STRONGER WINDS ALOFT /35-45 KT AT 500 MB/ WILL DEVELOP OVER CNTRL/ERN MT IN ASSOCIATION WITH EJECTING LEAD SHORTWAVE TROUGH. MID-UPPER FLOW OVER REMAINDER OF WARM SECTOR SHOULD REMAIN MODEST WITH 25-35 KT 0-6 KM SHEAR. STORMS WILL INTENSIFY AS THEY DEVELOP THROUGH THE DESTABILIZING WARM SECTOR. WEAK TO MODEST UPPER FLOW AND LARGE TEMPERATURE-DEWPOINT SPREADS WHERE THE STORMS INITIATE SUGGEST MOST OF THE ACTIVITY SHOULD BECOME OUTFLOW DOMINANT WITH LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND THE MAIN THREATS. A FEW SUPERCELL WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH INITIAL STORMS...ES

outlooks.summary: SCATTERED SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS WILL DEVELOP ACROSS THE CENTRAL AND NORTHERN HIGH PLAINS...FROM EASTERN MONTANA ACROSS THE WESTERN DAKOTAS AND NEBRASKA TO WESTERN KANSAS...NORTHEAST COLORADO...AND THE NORTHERN TEXAS PANHANDLE. LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND GUSTS WILL BE THE MAIN SEVERE THREATS PRIMARILY FROM MID AFTERNOON INTO THE EVENING HOURS.

sections.title: CENTRAL/NRN HIGH PLAINS THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING
sections.text: LEAD SPEED MAXIMA WILL EJECT NEWD TOWARD THE NRN ROCKIES/NRN HIGH PLAINS AS THE PRIMARY MIDLEVEL SHORTWAVE TROUGH PROGRESSES ESEWD OVER THE SRN GREAT BASIN. GRADUALLY INCREASING SWLY MIDLEVEL FLOW WILL CONTRIBUTE TO LEE CYCLOGENESIS ACROSS THE NRN HIGH PLAINS...WITH A LEE TROUGH/DRYLINE EXTENDING SWD INTO THE CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS. ALONG AND E OF THE LEE TROUGH...BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS IN THE 50S AND 60S WILL COMBINE WITH DAYTIME HEATING AND STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES TO RESULT IN MLCAPE VALUES OF 1500-3000 J/KG. THOUGH THE STRONGER MID/HIGH-LEVEL FLOW WILL NOT OVERLAP MUCH WITH THE MOIST SECTOR...FORECAST SOUNDINGS SHOW DEEP-LAYER VERTICAL SHEAR AT LEAST MARGINALLY FAVORABLE FOR SUPERCELLS OVER THE NRN HIGH PLAINS THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING...WITH SOMEWHAT WEAKER VERTICAL SHEAR FARTHER S INTO WRN KS. THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT APPEARS LIKELY IN A BROKEN BAND ALONG THE LEE TROUGH THIS AFTERNOON FROM ERN MT TO NE CO...WITH THE MORE WIDESPREAD CONVECTION EXPECTED ACROSS THE NRN HIGH PLAINS. THE INITIAL STORMS COULD EXHIBIT SUPERCELL STRUCTURE WITH AN ATTENDANT RISK FOR LARGE HAIL. THE SOMEWHAT WEAK FLOW ALOFT SUGGESTS THAT OUTFLOW MERGERS AND UPSCALE GROWTH INTO LINE SEGMENTS/CLUSTERS CAN

sections.title: INTERIOR CENTRAL/S FL THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: MODERATE INSTABILITY IS EXPECTED THIS AFTERNOON OVER INTERIOR FL AS SEA BREEZE CONVECTION DEVELOPS. STORMS WILL TEND TO MOVE SWD ALONG THE SEA BREEZE BOUNDARIES...WITH THE POTENTIAL FOR ISOLATED STRONG/DAMAGING DOWNBURST WINDS.

sections.title: TX COAST TO LOWER MS VALLEY TODAY
sections.text: A TROPICAL MOISTURE PLUME IMMEDIATELY E OF A WEAK MIDLEVEL TROUGH DRIFTING EWD INVOF NE TX/SE OK WILL SUPPORT SCATTERED-NUMEROUS THUNDERSTORMS FROM THE TX COAST NEWD INTO THE LOWER MS VALLEY. DEEP MOIST PROFILES AND WEAK VERTICAL SHEAR SUGGEST THAT SEVERE STORMS ARE UNLIKELY. ..THOMPSON/COOK.. 06/26/2014

ACROSS THE CENTRAL CONUS...A NUMBER OF WEAKER CONVECTIVELY INDUCED AND/OR SUSTAINED DISTURBANCES WILL LEAD THE STRONGER SHORTWAVE TROUGH AND DRIFT SLOWLY EAST TOWARD THE MS RIVER VALLEY THROUGH THE PERIOD. IN THE EAST...SOMEWHAT DRIER AIR WILL EVENTUALLY FOLLOW THE PASSAGE OF AN UPPER TROUGH ACROSS THE NORTHEAST WHILE TROPICAL AIRMASS PERSISTS ACROSS THE SOUTH.

sections.text: UPPER TROUGH AND ASSOCIATED WIND MAX WILL EJECT NEWD TOWARD THE ROCKIES/NRN HIGH PLAINS FROM THE GREAT BASIN THROUGH LATE TONIGHT. AS SWLY MID-LEVEL FLOW STRENGTHENS ACROSS THE CONTINENTAL DIVIDE...LEE CYCLOGENESIS OCCURS OVER THE NRN HIGH PLAINS AND A LEE TROUGH/DRYLINE WILL SHARPEN ACROSS THE CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS. ALONG AND E OF THE LEE TROUGH...BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS IN THE 50S AND 60S WILL COMBINE WITH DAYTIME HEATING AND STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES TO RESULT IN MLCAPE VALUES OF 1500-3000 J/KG. THOUGH THE STRONGER MID/HIGH-LEVEL FLOW AND HEIGHT FALLS WILL NOT OVERLAP SUBSTANTIALLY WITH THE MOIST AXIS...FORECAST SOUNDINGS SHOW DEEP-LAYER VERTICAL SHEAR AT LEAST MARGINALLY FAVORABLE FOR SUPERCELLS OVER THE NRN HIGH PLAINS THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING...WITH SOMEWHAT WEAKER VERTICAL SHEAR FARTHER S INTO WRN KS. STRONGER THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT APPEARS LIKELY IN A BROKEN BAND ALONG THE LEE TROUGH THIS AFTERNOON FROM MT TO NE CO...WITH THE MORE CONCENTRATED STORM COVERAGE EXPECTED ACROSS THE NRN HIGH PLAINS. INITIAL STORMS COULD EXHIBIT SUPERCELL STRUCTURE WITH AN ATTENDANT RISK FOR LARGE HAIL. GIVEN THE SOMEWHAT WEAKER FLOW ALOFT ACROSS THE AREA OF STORM INITIATION...EXPECT OUTFLOW MERG

sections.title: NRN/CENTRAL TO SRN PLAINS
sections.text: REMNANT MCV/S AND ASSOCIATED CLUSTERS OF CONVECTION ARE PRESENT THIS MORNING FROM THE ERN DAKOTAS SOUTH ACROSS NE/IA...AND S-CNTRL KS. SOME OF THESE STORMS ARE FORECAST TO PERSIST IN SCATTERED FASHION AMIDST WEAK WARM ADVECTION AND MODEST INSTABILITY. GENERALLY MEAGER SHEAR AND WEAK LAPSE RATES WITH EWD EXTENT SHOULD TEMPER ANY SEVERE WEATHER POTENTIAL WITH THIS ACTIVITY THROUGH THE DAY.

sections.title: INTERIOR CENTRAL/S FL THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: MODERATE INSTABILITY IS EXPECTED THIS AFTERNOON OVER INTERIOR FL AS SEA BREEZE CONVECTION DEVELOPS. STORMS WILL TEND TO MOVE SWD ALONG THE SEA BREEZE BOUNDARIES...WITH THE POTENTIAL FOR ISOLATED STRONG/DAMAGING DOWNBURST WINDS.

sections.title: TX/LA GULF COAST
sections.text: A TROPICAL MOISTURE PLUME IMMEDIATELY E OF A WEAK MIDLEVEL TROUGH DRIFTING EWD INVOF NE TX WILL SUPPORT SCATTERED-NUMEROUS THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS THE TX/LA GULF COAST. DEEP MOIST PROFILES AND WEAK VERTICAL SHEAR SUGGEST THAT MULTICELL STORMS ARE LIKELY TO PERSIST WITH A LOW PROBABILITY OF ISOLATED WET DOWNBURSTS. ..CARBIN/MARSH.. 06/26/2014

LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND GUSTS WILL BE THE MAIN SEVERE THREATS PRIMARILY FROM MID AFTERNOON INTO THE EVENING HOURS.

sections.title: CNTRL AND WRN KS...NWRN OK...SERN KS
sections.text: MESOSCALE SYSTEM OVER CNTRL KS HAS STABILIZED THE AIR MASS LOCALLY...THEREFORE HAVE TRIMMED THE SLIGHT RISK AREA WEST A BIT INTO WRN KS WHERE STRONGER HEATING WILL BREAK THE CAP. VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY SHOWS CU OVER SERN CO...WITH A VERY MOIST AND UNSTABLE AIR MASS SEWD INTO NWRN OK. THIS CORRIDOR COULD BE A FAVORED AREA FOR WIND AND HAIL TO DEVELOP LATER TODAY.

sections.title: NRN HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: HEATING CONTINUES TO DESTABILIZE THE AIR MASS WITH ELY SURFACE WINDS HELPING TO MAXIMIZE HODOGRAPH LENGTH DESPITE MODEST FLOW ALOFT. FORWARD PROPAGATING STORMS CAPABLE OF HAIL AND WIND ARE LIKELY AS CONVECTION MOVES OFF THE HIGHER TERRAIN. FOR MORE INFORMATION SEE MESOSCALE DISCUSSION 1158. ..JEWELL.. 06/26/2014 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1119 AM CDT THU JUN 26 2014/

outlooks.summary: SCATTERED STRONG TO SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS WILL PERSIST THROUGH MID EVENING FROM EASTERN MONTANA ACROSS THE WESTERN DAKOTAS AND NEBRASKA TO EASTERN COLORADO AND NORTHWESTERN KANSAS. MORE ISOLATED SEVERE STORMS MIGHT DEVELOP FROM SOUTHEASTERN COLORADO INTO SOUTHWEST KANSAS AND THE TEXAS AND OKLAHOMA PANHANDLES. LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND GUSTS WILL BE THE MAIN THREATS THIS EVENING BEFORE STORMS WEAKEN LATER TONIGHT.

sections.title: NRN THROUGH CNTRL HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: NUMEROUS STORMS THAT DEVELOPED OVER THE HIGHER TERRAIN CONTINUE THROUGH ERN MT...ERN WY AND NERN CO. STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO PERSIST INTO THE WRN DAKOTAS AND WRN NEB THIS EVENING. THE 00Z RAOB DATA AND OBJECTIVE ANALYSIS INDICATE 2000-3000 J/KG MLCAPE WHERE STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES HAVE OVERSPREAD WRN PORTION OF MOIST WARM SECTOR. WITH EXCEPTION OF ERN MT...VERTICAL SHEAR IN THIS REGION IS WEAK WITH 0-6 KM SHEAR AOB 30 KT. THUS STORM MODE IS EXPECTED TO REMAIN PRIMARILY MULTICELLULAR. TENDENCY SHOULD BE FOR MOST STORMS TO CONGEAL INTO CLUSTERS AND LINES AS COLD POOLS MERGE. THE 00Z RAOB DATA INDICATED AT LEAST A MODEST CAPPING INVERSION BETWEEN 700 AND 850 MB AT THE BASE OF THE EML...AND CONVECTIVE INHIBITION WILL INCREASE WITH NOCTURNAL COOLING. NEVERTHELESS...INCREASING STORM SCALE CONVERGENCE ASSOCIATED WITH THE STRENGTHENING LLJ INTERACTING WITH THE CONSOLIDATED COLD POOLS SHOULD SUSTAIN ACTIVITY INTO A PORTION OF THE HIGH PLAINS NEXT FEW HOURS. THE STRONGER STORMS WILL REMAIN CAPABLE OF PRODUCING STRONG TO DAMAGING WIND GUSTS AND HAIL. HOWEVER...STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO BEGIN A WEAKENING TREND AFTER 04Z AS THE BOUNDARY LAYER CONTINUES TO COOL AND CONVECTIVE INHIBITION STRENGTH

sections.title: SERN CO THROUGH SWRN KS AND THE TX AND OK PANHANDLES
sections.text: EXTENT OF THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT IN THIS REGION TONIGHT REMAINS UNCERTAIN...BUT WILL MAINTAIN A CONDITIONAL SLIGHT RISK NEVERTHELESS. AREA OF AGITATED CUMULUS THAT DEVELOPED OVER SERN CO WHERE A WWD MOVING OUTFLOW BOUNDARY INTERSECTED THE DRYLINE APPEARS TO BE ON THE DECREASE...WITH AN ORPHAN ANVIL ALSO EVIDENT. DEEPER FORCING FOR ASCENT ASSOCIATED WITH A PROGRESSIVE SHORTWAVE TROUGH WILL GRADUALLY SPREAD INTO THIS REGION AND OVERTAKE THE DRYLINE LATER THIS EVENING/TONIGHT. HOWEVER...THE 00Z RAOB FROM DODGE CITY ALSO SHOWED SUBSTANTIAL CAPPING INVERSION AROUND 700 MB...AND CONVECTIVE INHIBITION WILL INCREASE AS THE BOUNDARY LAYER COOLS. SHOULD STORMS INITIATE...THREAT WILL EXIST FOR LARGE HAIL AND STRONG TO DAMAGING GUSTS. SEE SWOMCD 1164 FOR MORE INFORMATION. ..DIAL.. 06/27/2014

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL AND STRONG WIND GUSTS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP ACROSS PARTS OF ERN MT AND ERN WY THIS AFTERNOON AND TRACK E/NE INTO THE WRN DAKOTAS THIS EVENING. A WATCH MAY BE NEEDED BY 20Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SHOWERS AND THUNDERSTORMS WERE BEGINNING TO DEVELOP OVER THE HIGHER TERRAIN OF WRN WY AS DEEP LAYER SHEAR INCREASES WITH THE APPROACH OF A LEAD SHORTWAVE IMPULSE EJECTING ACROSS SE ID/FAR WRN WY PER LATEST WV IMAGERY. A SFC TROUGH/DRYLINE WAS NOTED IN 18Z MESOANALYSIS EXTENDING SWD THROUGH CNTRL/ERN WY INTO ERN CO. SOUTHEASTERLY LOW LEVEL FLOW TO THE EAST OF THIS FEATURE HAS TRANSPORTED MID 50S TO MID 60S DEWPOINTS INTO ERN MT/WY AND THE WRN DAKOTAS. AS HEATING CONTINUES INTO THE 80S THIS AFTERNOON...WEAK CAPPING WILL ERODE AND SBCAPE VALUES AOA 2000 J/KG WILL BE POSSIBLE. STEEP LAPSE RATES AND EFFECTIVE 0-6 KM SHEAR VALUES WILL BE ADEQUATE FOR SOME SUPERCELL STRUCTURES CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL AND STRONG WIND GUSTS. STORMS MAY INITIALLY REMAIN ISOLATED BUT ARE EXPECTED TO INCREASE IN COVERAGE AND EVENTUALLY MAY GROW UPSCALE INTO AN E/NEWD ADVANCING MCS LATER THIS EVENING AS STORMS TRACK INTO THE WRN DAKOTAS/NE MT.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: STORMS CAPABLE OF HAIL AND STRONG WIND GUSTS WILL BE POSSIBLE ACROSS SE WY INTO THE NEB PANHANDLE...WITH A MORE ISOLATED THREAT INTO NE CO INTO THE EVENING HOURS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: TEMPERATURES HAVE WARMED INTO THE LOW/MID 80S THIS AFTERNOON TO THE EAST OF THE FRONT RANGE FROM SE WY INTO NE CO. 19Z MESOANALYSIS STILL INDICATED WEAK CAPPING ACROSS THE HIGH PLAINS...BUT WITH ADDITIONAL HEATING THIS SHOULD GRADUALLY ERODE ENOUGH THAT ISOLATED STORMS MAY DEVELOP/INTENSIFY IN THE VICINITY OF THE DRYLINE/LEE SFC TROUGH AND/OR MOVE OFF HIGHER TERRAIN. MODEST FORCING FOR ASCENT AND WEAKENING DEEP LAYER SHEAR WITH SOUTHWARD EXTENT INTO CO /LESS THAN 25 KT EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR/ SHOULD LIMIT STORM COVERAGE/ORGANIZATION. BUT GIVEN DEGREE OF INSTABILITY /A0A 2500 J PER KG MLCAPE/ AND STEEP LAPSE RATES...A THREAT OF HAIL AND STRONG WIND GUSTS WILL ACCOMPANY ANY STORMS THAT ARE ABLE TO DEVELOP AND BE SUSTAINED INTO THE HIGH PLAINS. THE BEST CHANCE FOR ORGANIZED SEVERE STORMS APPEARS TO BE OVER SE WY...EXTREME NE CO INTO THE NEB PANHANDLE WHERE BETTER BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE EXISTS ON THE PERIPHERY OF STRONGER DEEP LAYER SHEAR/FORCING FOCUSED FURTHER TO THE NORTH OVER NW WY. HERE...STORMS MAY EVENTUALLY EVOLVE INTO A NEWD PROGRESSING CLUSTER/BOWING SEGMENT INTO THE EVENING. FURTHER SOUTH ACROSS CO...WEAKER SHEAR/FORCING SHOULD LIMIT COVERAGE AND THE OVERALL THREAT.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: STRONG TO BRIEFLY SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS WILL CONTINUE TO DEVELOP ACROSS THE AREA THROUGH THE AFTERNOON. A WATCH IS CURRENTLY NOT ANTICIPATED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THUNDERSTORMS HAVE DEVELOPED ON THE NORTHERN PERIPHERY OF A COMPACT SHORT-WAVE TROUGH/MESOSCALE CONVECTIVE VORTEX MOVING ACROSS CENTRAL KANSAS. THE AMBIENT ENVIRONMENT THAT THESE THUNDERSTORMS ARE DEVELOPING WITHIN IS CHARACTERIZED BY STRONG INSTABILITY /MUCAPE VALUES GENERALLY BETWEEN 2500-4000 J/KG/...BUT RELATIVELY WEAK/MODEST DEEP-LAYER SHEAR. THE LACK OF BETTER DEEP-LAYER SHEAR SHOULD ACT TO LIMIT THE OVERALL POTENTIAL FOR ORGANIZED/WIDESPREAD SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS...BUT GIVEN THE DEGREE OF INSTABILITY...STRONG TO ISOLATED SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS WILL BE POSSIBLE. ISOLATED DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL WILL BE THE MAIN SEVERE THREATS WITH ANY THUNDERSTORM...ALTHOUGH WEAK/MODEST MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES /GENERALLY BETWEEN 6-6.5 C/KM/ WILL ACT TO LIMIT THE POTENTIAL FOR VERY LARGE HAIL. GIVEN THE ANTICIPATED BRIEF/SPOTTY NATURE OF THE SEVERE THREAT...A WATCH IS CURRENTLY NOT EXPECTED.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A FEW ISOLATED DMGG WIND GUSTS WILL REMAIN POSSIBLE INTO THE EARLY EVENING HOURS...BUT WW ISSUANCE IS NOT NEEDED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SEA-BREEZE-ENHANCED CONVECTION WILL CONTINUE TO REGENERATE OVER INTERIOR SECTIONS OF THE FLORIDA PENINSULA WHERE EARLIER STRONG INSOLATION AMIDST UPPER 60S/LOWER 70S SFC DEWPOINTS HAS SUPPORTED 1500-2500 J/KG OF MLCAPE. VIS IMAGERY AND MOSAIC RADAR DATA SUGGEST THE GREATEST CONCENTRATION OF THIS ACTIVITY LYING N OF A TAMPA-ORLANDO LINE WHERE COLD POOLS ARE AMALGAMATING...WITH MORE ISOLATED STORMS BLOSSOMING ALONG CLOUD-LINE-MANIFESTED CONVERGENCE ZONES FARTHER S. DURING THE NEXT FEW HOURS...ALL OF THIS ACTIVITY WILL GRADUALLY SPREAD SEWD/SWD...AIDED BY 20-25 KT OF FLOW IN THE 3-6-KM-AGL LAYER SAMPLED BY AREA VWPS. MODEST DEEP SHEAR ASSOCIATED WITH THIS FLOW MAY CONTINUE TO FOSTER SUSTAINED MULTICELL CLUSTERS WITH ISOLATED DMGG WIND GUSTS POSSIBLE...WITH THE CNTRL FL PENINSULA MOST LIKELY EXPERIENCING THIS ACTIVITY DURING THE NEXT COUPLE OF HOURS. HOWEVER...NOCTURNAL COOLING WILL MINIMIZE THE REMAINING DURATION OF THIS RISK...AND THE LACK OF STRONGER DEEP SHEAR SHOULD ALSO LIMIT THE DMGG-WIND RISK.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: LARGE HAIL/LOCALLY DAMAGING WIND GUST POTENTIAL CONTINUES PARTICULARLY ACROSS SOUTHEAST/EAST-CENTRAL MT AND NORTHEAST WY...IN ADDITION TO PORTIONS OF NORTH-CENTRAL WY/SOUTH-CENTRAL MT. SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH 357 CONTINUES UNTIL 03Z. A SEVERE RISK MAY SPREAD INTO WESTERN ND THROUGH EARLY/MID-EVENING...SUCH THAN AN ADDITIONAL SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH IS POSSIBLE /40 PERCENT CHANCE/.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST SURFACE ANALYSIS FEATURES A DEEPENING SURFACE LOW ACROSS EAST-CENTRAL WY/FAR SOUTHEAST MT...WITH A NORTHWARD-EXTENDING SURFACE TROUGH ACROSS EASTERN MT AND A SHARPENING WARM FRONTAL ZONE EXTENDING GENERALLY NORTHEAST-SOUTHEASTWARD ACROSS ND. COINCIDENT WITH THE LEADING EDGE OF WEAK HEIGHT FALLS...AND NEAR THE AFOREMENTIONED SURFACE LOW/TROUGH...STRONG/SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS CONTINUE TO DEVELOP EAST-NORTHEASTWARD ACROSS NORTHEAST WY/EASTERN MT. NEAR/EAST OF THESE STORMS...A RELATIVELY WARM/MOIST AIR MASS WITH SURFACE DEWPOINTS IN THE UPPER 50S/LOWER 60S F IS LIKELY CONTRIBUTING TO 2000-3500 J/KG MLCAPE ACROSS SOUTHEAST MT/FAR EASTERN WY INTO THE WESTERN SD/SOUTHWEST ND. 30-40 KT OF EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR WILL SUPPORT SUSTAINED MULTICELLS AND SOME SUPERCELLS WITH LARGE HAIL/LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS AS THE PRIMARY HAZARDS. INCREASING WARM ADVECTION THIS EVENING MAY HELP TO SUSTAIN STORMS EASTWARD INTO THE WESTERN DAKOTAS. FARTHER WEST...AN ADDITIONAL/SEPARATE CORRIDOR OF STORMS MAY INCREASE AND POSE A RELATIVELY ISOLATED SEVERE WIND/HAIL RISK ACROSS SOUTH-CENTRAL MT/CENTRAL WY. A 54 WIND GUST WAS RECENTLY MEASURED AT RIVERTON WY AS OF 2238Z. ..GUYER.. 06/26/2014 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ISOLATED LARGE HAIL/LOCALLY DAMAGING WIND RISK CONTINUES ACROSS SOUTHEAST WY/NORTHEAST CO INTO FAR WESTERN PORTIONS OF SD/NEB PANHANDLE THROUGH EARLY/MID-EVENING. SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH 358 CONTINUES UNTIL 03Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: MULTIPLE WIDELY SCATTERED CLUSTERS OF STORMS CONTINUE TO PROGRESS GENERALLY EASTWARD WITHIN A CORRIDOR ACROSS FAR EASTERN WY AND NORTHEAST CO /SOUTHWARD TO THE I-70 VICINITY NORTHWEST OF LIMON/ AS OF 2345Z. WHILE MOST ARE NOT PARTICULARLY INTENSE AT THIS TIME...GENERAL EASTWARD STORM PERSISTENCE SHOULD OCCUR INTO A RELATIVELY MOIST/UNSTABLE AIR MASS /2000+ J PER KG MLCAPE/ ACROSS REMAINING PORTIONS OF NORTHEAST CO/NEB PANHANDLE/WESTERN SD. AIDED BY DEEPENING SURFACE LOWS ACROSS EAST-CENTRAL WY AND SOUTHEAST CO...REGIONAL SURFACE DATA/WSR-88D VWP TRENDS DEPICT A BACKING/STRENGTHENING OF LOW-LEVEL WINDS...WITH ASSOCIATED RAMIFICATIONS FOR AN INCREASING UPSLOPE COMPONENT/STORM-RELATIVE INFLOW AND PROBABLE STORM PERSISTENCE. ALTHOUGH A MID/HIGH-LEVEL FLOW WEAKNESS IS APPARENT...LOW-LEVEL VEERING IS CONTRIBUTING TO AS MUCH AS 30-40 KT OF EFFECTIVE SHEAR...WHICH WILL ALLOW FOR TRANSIENT SUPERCELLS AND A MORE PREVALENT TREND OF SEMI-ORGANIZED LINEAR CLUSTERS. THESE STORMS WILL BE CAPABLE OF LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS AND BOUTS OF LARGE HAIL THROUGH EARLY/MID-EVENING. ..GUYER.. 06/26/2014 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE AREA IS BEING MONITORED FOR A POSSIBLE INCREASE IN THE POTENTIAL FOR SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS THIS EVENING. IT IS POSSIBLE THAT THIS MAY WARRANT WW ISSUANCE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: FOCUSED MESOSCALE CONVERGENCE AT THE INTERSECTION OF A DRYLINE EXTENDING SWD FROM 997-MB SFC LOW PRESSURE ANALYZED 35 SSE PUB AND AN OUTFLOW BOUNDARY EXTENDING E/ESE OF THE LOW IS COLLOCATED WITH INCREASINGLY AGITATED CUMULUS IN SERN CO PER VIS IMAGERY. EARLIER CONVECTIVE PROCESSING TO THE W OF A SECONDARY DRYLINE /ANALYZED AROUND 60-80 MILES TO THE E OF THE FIRSTLY MENTIONED DRYLINE/ HAS CONTRIBUTED TO BOUNDARY-LAYER MOISTENING WWD TO THE AFOREMENTIONED LOW. THIS IS PARTICULARLY THE CASE N OF THE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY WHERE DEWPOINTS INCREASED AROUND 10F IN AN HOUR FOLLOWING THE WWD FLUX OF CONVECTIVELY MODIFIED AIR AT LA JUNTA AND LAMAR. WITH THIS MOISTURE BACKING WWD OVER ANTECEDENT NEARLY DRY ADIABATIC SFC-3-KM LAPSE RATES...AT LEAST MARGINAL BUOYANCY EXISTS E OF THE WRN DRYLINE. CONVECTION MAY CONTINUE TO BLOSSOM WITHIN THIS REGIME -- MOST LIKELY NEAR/E OF THE SFC CYCLONE -- AS LARGE-SCALE ASCENT INCREASES FROM THE W PER WATER VAPOR IMAGERY. HIGH DCAPE -- I.E. 1500-2000 J/KG -- WILL SUPPORT STRONG DOWNBURSTS WITH SVR WIND GUSTS POSSIBLE...AND SVR HAIL MAY ALSO OCCUR GIVEN 35-50 KT OF EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR AMIDST STEEP LOW/MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES. HIGH LCLS WILL MITIGATE THE TORNADO RISK DESPITE ENHANCED LOW-LEVEL SHEAR/VERTICAL VORTICITY INVOF THE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY. IF CONGEALING COLD POOLS WERE TO BREED UPSCALE CONVECTIVE GROWTH SUPPORTING A CORRIDOR OF SVR-WIND RISK...THE ISSUANCE OF A WW MAY BECOME NECESSARY. THIS COULD BE ENCOURAGED BY THE STRENGTHENING OF A LLJ OVER THE GREAT PLAINS. HOWEVER...LIMITED LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE -- ESPECIALLY W OF THE SECONDARY/ERN DRYLINE -- MAY MITIGATE SUCH POTENTIAL. ALSO...WITH UPCOMING NOCTURNAL COOLING DEPLETING SFC-BASED BUOYANCY...AND EVEN STRONGER DCVA LAGGING TO THE W...THERE ARE MULTIPLE FACTORS LIMITING THE OVERALL SVR RISK.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: LOCALLY DAMAGING WIND/ISOLATED LARGE HAIL RISK WILL LIKELY CONTINUE TO DEVELOP INTO FAR NORTHWEST KS AND WEST/SOUTHWEST NEB THIS EVENING. WHILE THE MAGNITUDE/EXTENSIVENESS OF THE SEVERE RISK IS A BIT UNCERTAIN...CONVECTIVE TRENDS ARE BEING MONITORED FOR A POSSIBLE SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: MULTIPLE SMALL LINEAR SEGMENTS CONTINUE TO PROGRESS EAST-NORTHEASTWARD ACROSS THE NEB PANHANDLE AND NORTHEAST CO AS OF 0145Z. IN ASSOCIATION WITH THE NORTHEAST CO CLUSTER...A 52 KT WIND GUST WAS MEASURED IN FORT MORGAN CO JUST PRIOR TO 01Z...WITH A 44 KT MEASURED GUST AT AKRON CO AT 0106Z. THE DOWNSTREAM/INFLOW AIR MASS TO THE EAST-SOUTHEAST REMAINS RELATIVELY WARM/UNSTABLE WITH MODEST CINH AND MLCAPE LIKELY IN EXCESS OF 2000+ J/KG BASED ON REGIONAL 00Z OBSERVED SOUNDINGS AND SPC OBJECTIVE ANALYSIS. REGIONAL DERIVED WIND DATA /SUCH AS GOODLAND WSR-88D VWP/ REFLECT AN INCREASING SOUTH-SOUTHEASTERLY LOW-LEVEL JET EARLY THIS EVENING...WITH ASSOCIATED WARM ADVECTION/STORM RELATIVE INFLOW CONTRIBUTING TO AN EAST-NORTHEASTWARD PERSISTENCE OF STRONGER-CALIBER STORMS THIS EVENING. LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS/ISOLATED INSTANCES OF LARGE HAIL WILL REMAIN POSSIBLE INTO LATE EVENING...AND A NEW SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH IS POSSIBLE PENDING INCREASING ORGANIZATIONAL/INTENSITY TRENDS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE THREAT FOR DAMAGING WINDS AND SEVERE HAIL IS EXPECTED TO PERSIST BEYOND THE SCHEDULED 03Z EXPIRATION OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCHES 357 AND 358. AS SUCH...A NEW SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH OR LOCAL WFO EXTENSION MAY BE REQUIRED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A LOOSELY ORGANIZED MCS OVER NERN WY HAS RECENTLY INTENSIFIED NEAR AND JUST EAST OF THE BLACK HILLS IN WRN SD WITH A WIND GUST TO 67 MPH OBSERVED IN SPEARFISH. IT APPEARS THAT THE COLD POOL ATTENDANT TO THIS CONVECTIVE SYSTEM HAS BECOME SUFFICIENTLY STRONG AND DEEP TO TAP THE MOIST AND MODERATELY UNSTABLE BOUNDARY LAYER SAMPLED BY THE 00Z RAPID CITY SOUNDING. CURRENT RADAR DATA SUGGEST THAT THE COLD POOL HAS SURGED WELL AHEAD OF THE CONVECTIVE TOWERS...CASTING SOME UNCERTAINTY ON THE SUBSEQUENT EVOLUTION OF THE MCS. A RAPID INTENSIFICATION OF THE NOCTURNAL LLJ IS ANTICIPATED WITHIN THE NEXT HOUR OR TWO WHICH COULD POTENTIALLY BALANCE THE SURGING COLD POOL AND ENHANCE MORE UPRIGHT UPDRAFT GROWTH IN CLOSER PROXIMITY TO THE GUST FRONT. SHOULD THIS SCENARIO UNFOLD...A LONGER DURATION DAMAGING WIND AND SEVERE HAIL EVENT MAY PERSIST ACROSS PORTIONS OF WRN SD...POSSIBLY INTO SWRN ND. FARTHER TO THE WEST...A SECONDARY BAND OF ASCENT APPEARS TO BE MOVING THROUGH THE BIG HORN BASIN...ENHANCING DOWNSHEAR STORM DEVELOPMENT OVER NERN WY INTO SERN MT. WHILE ISOLATED SEVERE STORMS ARE POSSIBLE WITH THIS SECONDARY CONVECTIVE REGIME...ANTECEDENT CONVECTIVE OVERTURNING BY THE WRN SD STORMS SHOULD LIMIT SEVERE STORM COVERAGE.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS AND BOUTS OF SEVERE HAIL WILL REMAIN POSSIBLE THROUGH THE EARLY PART OF THE OVERNIGHT ACROSS FAR NORTHEAST CO AND WEST/SOUTHWEST NEB. SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH 359 CONTINUES UNTIL 07Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A FRAGMENTED QUASI-LINEAR COMPLEX CONTINUES TO MOVE EAST-NORTHEASTWARD NEAR THE CO/NEB/KS BORDER VICINITY AS OF 0430Z...WITH AN ACCELERATING BOWING SEGMENT /40+ KT FORWARD MOTION/ NOTED ACROSS YUMA COUNTY CO. ANOTHER SMALLER CLUSTER OF STORMS IS ONGOING ACROSS THE NORTHERN NEB PANHANDLE /INCLUDING AN APPARENT HEAT BURST NOTED IN THE SCOTTSBLUFF VICINITY AS OF 04Z/. A STRONG SOUTH-SOUTHEASTERLY LOW-LEVEL JET...READILY NOTED IN WSR-88D VWP DATA FROM GOODLAND/NORTH PLATTE/DODGE CITY...CONTINUES TO SUPPORT QUASI-LINEAR STORM SUSTENANCE VIA WARM ADVECTION/STORM-RELATIVE INFLOW. THE BOUNDARY LAYER HAS DECOUPLED OVER THE PAST COUPLE OF HOURS AS SURFACE TEMPERATURES HAVE STEADILY COOLED THROUGH THE 70S F. A CONTINUED TREND OF INCREASINGLY ELEVATED/SOMEWHAT MORE STABLE INFLOW SHOULD RESULT IN A GRADUAL TEMPERING OF CONVECTIVE INTENSITY OVERNIGHT...ALTHOUGH LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS AND ISOLATED BOUTS OF SEVERE HAIL WILL REMAIN POSSIBLE EARLY IN THE OVERNIGHT. ..GUYER.. 06/27/2014 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A MARGINAL SEVERE THREAT MAY CONTINUE FOR ANOTHER HOUR OR TWO ACROSS SCNTRL NEB AND NW KS. HAIL AND STRONG GUSTY WINDS WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH THE MORE INTENSE CELLS. DUE TO THE ISOLATED NATURE OF THE THREAT...ADDITIONAL WW ISSUANCE IS NOT EXPECTED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST MESOANALYSIS SHOWS A CORRIDOR OF MODERATE INSTABILITY EXTENDING NWD ACROSS WRN KS INTO SW NEB. A SHORT BOWING LINE SEGMENT IS LOCATED ON THE NRN END OF THE STRONGER INSTABILITY AND IS LOCATED NEAR THE NOSE OF A 45 TO 55 KT LOW-LEVEL JET. THE INSTABILITY AND STRONG LOW-LEVEL FLOW WILL HELP MAINTAIN THE LINE FOR A FEW MORE HOURS. THE MODIFIED NORTH PLATTE 00Z SOUNDING SUGGESTS THAT THE CONVECTION IS NOT SUBSTANTIALLY SFC-BASED. AS THE LINE MOVES ENEWD...THIS TREND FOR THE CONVECTION TO BECOME ELEVATED SHOULD MAKE THE SEVERE THREAT MORE MARGINAL WITH TIME. STILL...STRONG WIND GUSTS AND POSSIBLY MARGINALLY SEVERE GUSTS MAY BE ASSOCIATED WITH THE LEADING EDGE OF THE LINE FOR ANOTHER HOUR OR TWO.
